Athena++ audit · BSG envelope · 2026-10-15

Why Linhao's BSG collapses and ours does not

Run in the same 1-D setup (his initial profile, his inner boundary, the same tables), Athena++ loses energy near the base within days and the envelope deflates. Our AthenaK radiation module (rad_m1) stays stable for 30 days. An energy ledger names the sink: Athena++'s implicit radiation iteration stops before it converges, and the gas is charged with flux divergences that do not add up between neighbouring cells. At the optically thick base cells that mismatch destroys energy.

Athena++ main branch e47fabb7. AthenaK fin51-linhao-bc d67d2599. Work directory /raven/ptmp/jinma/athpp_audit_1015.

Athena++: collapsesThe inner wall cools from 1.05e6 K to 2–5e5 K. The flux at the wall turns inward, pouring 100–400 L into the bath. The star loses 3–9e46 erg (100–300 × L·t). With angle_flag 1, the radius at ρ = 1e-10 g/cc shrinks from 54 to 45 R☉ by 17 d.
AthenaK: stable for 30 dThe wall temperature changes by only +0.8 %. The Fe bump stays quiet (|v| ≤ 3.7 km/s, ⟨T⟩ steady at 1.75e5 K). The outer radius settles at 51.5–52.5 R☉. Our positivity floors never fire.
Cause: an unconverged radiation iterationAthena++'s Jacobi iteration hits its 100-sweep limit at a relative change of about 1e-5, above its 1e-6 target. The gas is charged with the last sweep's flux divergence, which does not telescope, and 89 % of the loss sits in the first three cells. Converging the iteration stops the loss. His heat bath adds a real radiative drain on top.

Detail figures: wall cells, energy budgets and radial profiles

What differs between the codes

  1. Energy loss near the base (main driver, revised). Athena++ loses 3–5e46 erg in 5 d, all of it inside r < 30 R☉, while 0.02–0.03 M☉ moves inward into the first R☉. The inward cell-0 flux (−50 to −200 L) is mostly advective, (4/3) v E carried by gas falling at about 1 km/s, not a leak into the bath. The boundary-swap test (below) shows the boundary is not the cause.
  2. Per-angle RHS clip (confirmed Athena++ bug, amplifier). rad_source.cpp:132–135 clips each angle's pre-solve right-hand side to TINY_NUMBER. The gas is billed with the unclipped flux divergence (:447–461). The created radiation is paid for by cooling the gas. A minimal 1-D slab with a sharp τ jump gives L_out = 10.5 × L_in (athena/src/pgen/thickslab.cpp). In the BSG it halves the drain but does not remove it.
  3. angle_flag 0 in spherical-polar (second candidate). With the Athena++ default, the whole envelope accelerates inward at 50–70 cm/s² (8–10 % of g) within 0.1 d, for every taucell from 1 to 5. angle_flag 1 removes it. We do not know which setting he used.
  4. taucell force deficit (secondary). In thick cells the face flux carries an extra 3/(8·taucell) of L (9.5 % at taucell 4). The radiation force uses only the cell-centred flux, so near-Eddington gas loses 9.5 % of its radiative support. This builds up over a diffusion time and is too slow to matter in the first 30 d.
  5. Unverifiable without his deck. His time unit uses the hydrogen mass where Athena++ uses the atomic mass unit, which could make GM 0.78 % too strong. His iteration limits are unknown. His pgen also calls a function no public Athena++ has, so he runs a modified fork.

taucell 4 by itself barely matters. In 1-D his setup diverges within half a day for taucell ≥ 10, so 4 is probably what kept his run alive.

Each Athena++ ingredient was added to AthenaK as an opt-in debug key (branch athpp-emul-1015; with every key off the 30-day run is bitwise identical to the baseline) and switched on one at a time in the same 1-D setup. None of them, alone or in pairs, reproduces the collapse.

Revised conclusion. The collapse is an energy sink inside Athena++'s update near the optically thick base, present with any inner boundary. The ledger below names it.

Energy ledger: where the energy goes

A diagnostics-only copy of Athena++ records the energy change from every operator in every cell. Switching the ledger on leaves the run bit-for-bit identical, and it closes against the measured total to 1e-11. Totals below are changes since t = 0 in 1e45 erg for the full sphere.

RuntMeasured ΔE_totNon-telescoping radiation transportRadiation through the boundaryHydroGravityResets + floors
Closed flux wall, angle_flag 15 d−47.4−47.8+0.30.00.0+0.1
Closed flux wall, angle_flag 110 d−98.1−98.6+0.30.0−0.2+0.3
His boundary, taucell 4, angle_flag 05 d−37.7−12.0−25.8 (drain into the bath)00+0.1
  • Where. In the closed-wall run, 89 % of the non-telescoping loss at 5 d sits in cells 0–2 (−22.3, −12.2 and −8.0), all of it within cells 0–10.
  • When. It starts at about 0.05 d and keeps growing: −0.1 at 0.17 d, −1.0 at 1 d, −7.8 at 2 d, −48 at 5 d, −99 at 10 d.
  • Why. 17 of 18 sampled solves stop at nlimit = 100 with a relative change of about 1e-5, above error_limit = 1e-6. GetHydroSourceTerms then charges the gas with the last sweep's flux divergence, whose neighbour intensities come from the previous iterate, so the face fluxes do not cancel between cells.
  • Test with a converged iteration (error_limit 1e-11, up to 5000 sweeps; it converges in 1000–1700). The non-telescoping term stays at zero. At 2 d the converged run has gained +0.43e45 erg, while the default run with nlimit = 100 has lost 7.61e45 erg, of which 7.62e45 is non-telescoping transport. Converged runs cost about 13 CPU-hours per day of star time, so the test stops at 2 d.
  • Re-billing does not help. Recomputing the divergence from the final intensities before charging the gas makes the base unstable within 200 s (dt drops to 2.5e-10 s). The cure is a converged iteration, not a different way of charging an unconverged one.
  • Gravity, hydro fluxes, resets and floors conserve globally. The large local gravity term near the wall is mass moving in the potential and sums to about zero over the domain.

Conclusion of the ledger. In his default run, Athena++'s implicit radiation solve, stopped at nlimit = 100 before it converges, destroys energy in the optically thick base cells; with his heat bath, a radiative drain into the boundary adds to it.

Fixing the convergence in Athena++

A new opt-in option, radiation/sweep = 2 (default 0 leaves Athena++ bitwise unchanged), replaces the lagged Jacobi iteration with a direct block-tridiagonal solve of the full per-angle system along each radial line, followed by one ordinary sweep. It adds a per-cell convergence test, two Newton steps on the quartic temperature root, and telescoping billing of the gas from the converged intensities. 10 files, +440 lines, in our copy only (branch conv-fix, not pushed).

RunNon-telescoping lossCost (solve CPU per star day)Outcome
Closed wall, default−7.84e45 erg by 2 d28 sloses energy, deflates
Closed wall, converged reference0108 sblows up at 2.68 d
Closed wall, fix08 sblows up at 2.70 d
His boundary (angle_flag 0), fix026 sbath drains −31e45 erg by 5 d; deflates to 40 R☉, blows out ~18 d
His boundary (angle_flag 1), fix07 sdt collapses at 9 d

Final conclusion. The fix removes the energy destroyed by the unconverged iteration, at a third of the default cost. The BSG still does not survive in Athena++: once the solve is converged, the discretisation itself is unstable at the optically thick wall (the near-central thick-limit face flux plus a cell thermal/opacity runaway: cell 0 heats while cell 2 turns cold and dense), and his heat bath genuinely drains energy. The default run only lasted as long as it did because its unconverged billing was draining energy out of the base. Our implicit M1 solve has neither problem, which is why the same star is stable in AthenaK.

Caveats

  • The Athena++ input file is a reconstruction (nmu 4, nlimit 100, error 1e-6, CFL 0.3); his actual deck and fork are unknown.
  • AthenaK runs on an 8×8 wedge with no perturbation, because a true 1-D mesh is refused by implicit_vimp.
  • Cell-centre radii differ by 1–2 % between the codes (centroid convention), so the starting wall ρ and T differ by up to about 2 %.
  • The 1-D energy drain is far larger than his 3-D one (about 1e45 erg per wedge by 25 d), so his settings clearly change how fast it happens.
  • In K1 the energy budget closes only to 30 % (ΔE_tot +1.6e45 against ∫(L_in − L_top) dt of +2.3e45). The gap sits in the history-file diagnostic, not in the physics.
